cand.title: Started a second industrial building and equipment expansion in Tlajomulco totaling MXN 1 billion; completion is scheduled for December 2027.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Kattya R., Purchasing & Foreign Trade Manager at Daido Metal Mexico, is the strongest operational routing candidate because her profile explicitly covers services, supplier selection and supplier contracts. Yasuo Hibi is identified by the municipality as President of Daido Metal México and is a potential executive referral/sponsor. Neither is verified as the hotel buyer. Tomomitsu Furukawa, global President and COO, is a project sponsor rather than an established lodging contact.
findings.futureEdition: No future event edition is verified. Construction began in October 2026 and was already underway in the municipal bulletin dated 18 October; that bulletin date is not independently established as the ceremony date. Scheduled construction completion is December 2027, and production is planned for 2028, with no month published. The project therefore extends into the November 2026–May 2028 horizon, but no opening ceremony or travel dates within that horizon are confirmed.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference: pursue visiting executives, engineers, equipment-vendor personnel and off-site project meetings, not an Expo-attendee block. The reported Mexico/Japan/US collaboration supports a cross-border travel hypothesis but publishes no travelers or room nights. Sheraton Guadalajara Expo’s city business-hotel amenities, laundry and meeting facilities suit such visits conditionally. Its Expo adjacency is not a demonstrated advantage for this plant-based project; plant transport, stay lengths and rate tolerance must be qualified. No resort or incentive requirement is evidenced.
findings.venueCommitments: The expansion is committed to DMM’s existing industrial premises on Carretera San Isidro Mazatepec, Tlajomulco. The groundbreaking was at the plant. This is an industrial-site commitment, not a hotel booking, meeting-venue contract or room block.
findings.historicalRotation: Not an edition-based or rotating destination programme. The sourced historical activity is a one-time groundbreaking at the existing plant in October 2026; no destination rotation or recurring event cycle is established.
findings.accommodationSourcing: UNKNOWN / hotel_sourcing_unconfirmed. Reviewed project disclosures identify no accommodation RFP, incumbent hotel, booking agency, TMC, PCO, room block or booking deadline. Kattya R.’s current purchasing profile includes service sourcing and supplier-contract negotiation, making purchasing a plausible routing point; hotel/travel remit and signing authority remain unverified.
findings.organizationStructure: Corporate industrial account: Daido Metal Mexico, S.A. de C.V. (DMM), part of Daido Metal Co., Ltd.; not an association or identified PCO/DMC. Correct the seed website: daido.co.jp/en is DAIDO STEEL, whereas the relevant company website is daidometal.com. Material scope correction: the parent’s August 2026 disclosure specifies generator-engine bearings for data centers under a North American customer production commitment, rather than merely an automotive expansion. It describes approximately ¥4 billion for the building plus separate equipment investment; the municipality reports MXN 1 billion total, split equally between infrastructure and equipment. Do not equate these differently scoped budgets.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No sourced incumbent hotel, competitor room block, sell-out or overflow evidence was found. Industrial activity is at the Tlajomulco site, not Expo Guadalajara. Sheraton’s official page says it does not provide shuttle service; plant transfers would need separate validation/arrangement. No commute time or quantified location disadvantage is established.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach purchasing through the published Mexico switchboard +52-33-1454-5000 and/or Kattya R.’s professional profile; request the actual travel/administration or project-mobility owner. Use Yasuo Hibi only as a referral/sponsorship route if needed. Ask for November 2026–May 2028 visitor waves, vendor-paid versus company-paid stays, incumbent/TMC arrangements, rate caps, lengths of stay and plant-transfer requirements. Offer a site visit and conditional corporate/project rate plus small meeting options only after those needs are confirmed; do not create a speculative room block.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Reject the October 2026 groundbreaking as an expired one-time event for the requested horizon. The continuing expansion is a corporate-account prospect, not an accessible confirmed event block. Hotel sourcing remains unknown, not open and not proven closed.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: qualify project-related stays during construction/equipment installation through the scheduled December 2027 completion and the planned 2028 production start. The production month is unknown, so do not promise launch demand by May 2028. This is prospective corporate capture, not verified annual recurrence, overflow or a future event edition.
